reason: Conversation 2 sensibly proved the socket and reset, then honestly narrowed the fault to the machine (mains filter first, then wiring, then the board's power supply) while admitting it could not be certain. It respected the customer's refusal to open panels, sent him to a Candy/Haier or independent engineer, raised warranty and extended-cover checks, and held back from naming a part because no parts match was confirmed. Conversation 1 gave disjointed, repetitive replies that ignored what the customer said (it re-asked about the plug after a lamp had already proved the socket, and mentioned a blown fuse when the fuse was fine). It never reached a diagnosis, never suggested an engineer or warranty check, and left the customer asking 'what next?' with no useful answer. Conversation 2 does slightly over-favour the filter and floats insurance cover, but only as something to check, not as certain surge damage.
